prior_approach.content: Recent experiments and simulations confirmed the alloy has low stacking fault energy.
prior_approach.evidence_span: recent experiment [41] and simulations [37] [41] have confirmed that it indeed has a low staking fault energy of ∼20 mJ m −2

prior_approach.content: The CoCrFeMnNi HEA was synthesized using a previously reported gas-atomization method.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The polycrystalline CoCrFeMnNi HEA in our work was synthesized by a previously reported gas-atomization method [34] .

prior_limitation.content: No polymorphic transition has been observed in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA despite extensive study at ambient pressure.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: to our knowledge, no polymorphic transition has been observed.

causal_claim.content: Applying in situ high-pressure synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction revealed a polymorphic transition from fcc to hcp structure.
causal_claim.evidence_span: by employing in situ high-pressure synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction, we reveal a polymorphic transition from face-centred-cubic ( fcc ) structure to hexagonal-close-packing ( hcp ) structure

causal_claim.content: Increasing pressure significantly increases the critical transition temperature for the hcp-to-fcc transformation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Once the pressure was increased, the critical transition temperature significantly increased

causal_claim.content: High pressure helps overcome the kinetic barrier between hcp and fcc phases, enabling the polymorphic transition.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The polymorphic transition from fcc to hcp unveiled in this work demonstrates that high-pressure can help overcome the kinetic barrier between hcp and fcc HEAs.

mechanism_principle.content: The transition mechanism is attributed to the similarity in stacking sequence where hcp can be obtained from fcc via stacking faults, facilitated by low stacking fault energy.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The hcp structure can be readily obtained locally from a fcc structure by introducing stacking faults. And it can be easily realized in the current HEA because recent experiment [41] and simulations [37] [41] have confirmed that it indeed has a low staking fault energy of ∼20 mJ m −2

hypothesis_statement.content: The fcc phase is a thermodynamically metastable polymorph obtained by kinetic constraints, while the hcp structure is the thermodynamically favorable state but difficult to attain.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Our findings indicate that this fcc HEA is a thermodynamically metastable polymorph obtained by kinetic constraints and the thermodynamically favourable hcp structure is relatively difficult to attain.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose a phase boundary based on the determined critical transition temperatures at different pressures.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Based on four critical transition temperatures determined at different pressures, a boundary is proposed in Fig. 3b .

hypothesis_statement.content: The stacking fault energy diminishes with decreasing temperature, facilitating the sliding needed for the phase transition.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This observation indicates that the stacking fault energy may diminish with decreasing temperature, which could facilitate the sliding needed for a displacive phase transition from fcc to hcp

hypothesis_statement.content: The polymorphic transition behavior is expected to be general across various HEAs under specific pressure and temperature conditions.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The polymorphic transition discovered in this work is by no means limited to this specific CoCrFeMnNi HEA, and we expect that this behaviour could be general in various HEAs at certain pressure and temperature conditions.

evidence_result.content: The hcp phase was successfully synthesized at ambient conditions after the fcc-to-hcp transition occurred under hydrostatic compression.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the hcp phase could be retained when the pressure was totally released, which is the first synthesis of the CoCrFeMnNi HEA with an hcp structure at ambient conditions.

evidence_result.content: The CoCrFeMnNi HEA sample retains an fcc single-phase structure up to 19.5 GPa before undergoing a phase transition.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The initial HEA sample has an fcc single-phase structure, which remains stable up to 19.5 GPa.

evidence_result.content: A phase transition to a new phase occurs when pressure approaches 22.1 GPa.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Once the pressure approaches 22.1 GPa, extra diffraction peaks beside the (111) peak of fcc appeared (indicated by red triangles in Fig. 1c ), suggesting the occurrence of a phase transition.

evidence_result.content: The new phase formed under high pressure is identified as an hcp lattice.
evidence_result.evidence_span: All the new phase peaks were well indexed as crystallographic reflections of an hcp lattice (space group P6 3 /mmc ), which revealed an fcc -to- hcp transition under high-pressure in the prototype CoCrFeMnNi HEA

evidence_result.content: The fcc-to-hcp phase transition is irreversible upon decompression.
evidence_result.evidence_span: During decompression, surprisingly the phase transition was irreversible. The newly formed phase was completely retained down to ambient pressure.

evidence_result.content: The hcp phase remains stable up to 633 K at ambient pressure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The hcp phase remained stable up to 633 K at ambient pressure

evidence_result.content: Heating the hcp phase to 723 K at ambient pressure causes a transformation back to the fcc phase.
evidence_result.evidence_span: and almost completely transformed back to fcc when heated up to 723 K ( Supplementary Fig. 5 ).

evidence_result.content: At 26 GPa, the fcc phase begins to grow when the hcp phase is heated above approximately 1,400 K.
evidence_result.evidence_span: With continuous heating above ∼1,400 K at 26 GPa, the fcc phase started to gradually grow at the expense of the hcp phase.

evidence_result.content: Repeated experiments showed that decompression from different maximum pressures successfully obtains fcc/hcp composites with tunable fractions.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Decompression from different maximum pressures between ∼22 and ∼41 GPa in our repeated experiments successfully obtains fcc / hcp composites with tunable fractions after pressure release.

constraint.content: The gasket was constrained to a specific pre-indented thickness to define the sample chamber geometry.
constraint.evidence_span: The gasket was T301 stainless steel that was pre-indented down to a thickness of ∼42 μm.

constraint.content: The experiment was constrained by the pressure fluctuation limit of less than 0.2 GPa before and after exposure.
constraint.evidence_span: The pressure fluctuation estimated before and after each exposure was found to be less than 0.2 GPa.

contradiction.content: Dual-phase composites of fcc and hcp have never been observed in an equiatomic multicomponent HEA system with maximized entropy, contrary to the findings of this work.
contradiction.evidence_span: However, no such dual phase composite has ever been observed in an equiatomic multicomponent HEA system with maximization entropy.
